study_type_evidence.quote: Groups of mice were subcutaneously injected with rhG-CSF, PEG10k-rhG-CSF and C15-rhG-CSF at a single dose of 1.0 mg rhG-CSF/kg body weight.
The in vitro bioactivity of C15-rhG-CSF was determined by NFS-60 cell proliferation using the ... (MTT) assay.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: KM (Kunming) mice, male, 16-20 g; age not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: KM mice (male, 16–20 g) were purchased from the Experimental Animal Center of Shandong (Jinan, China).

in_vitro_detail: NFS-60 murine myeloblastic cell proliferation (MTT) bioactivity assay in RPMI-1640 with 12.5% horse serum and 2.5% FBS; plus cell-free physicochemical characterization (RP-HPLC, MALDI-TOF-MS, 1H NMR, circular dichroism).

agents.name: C15-rhG-CSF (rhG-CSF site-specifically conjugated at Cys18 with 1-pentadecyl-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione, C15-MAL)
agents.sequence_source: Body states only that rhG-CSF 'has 175 amino acid residues with a molecular weight of 18.8 kDa' and identifies Cys18 and Lys17/24/35/41; no amino-acid sequence is printed.

agents.dose: 1.0 mg rhG-CSF/kg body weight single dose (PK); 0.5 mg/kg (low dose) and 1.0 mg/kg (high dose) single dose (efficacy)

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Pharmacokinetic profiles of rhG-CSF, PEG10k-rhG-CSF and C15-rhG-CSF.
concentration_time_figure.note: The body states 'The rhG-CSF serum concentration–time curves and the pharmacokinetic parameters were shown in Figure 7 and Table 1', i.e. Figure 7 plots serum concentration versus time after a single 1.0 mg/kg subcutaneous dose for all three agents.

bioanalytical_method: Human G-CSF DuoSet ELISA Kit (R&D Systems); pharmacokinetic parameters calculated with DAS 2.0 software
bioanalytical_quote: The rhG-CSF concentrations of plasma samples were measured using Human G-CSF DuoSet ELISA Kit (R&D Systems, Inc. United States)
notes: Full PK parameter set is given in Table 1 for all three agents after a single 1.0 mg/kg s.c. dose in male KM mice: T1/2 2.74 ± 0.33 h (rhG-CSF), 13.05 ± 0.45 h (PEG10k-rhG-CSF), 5.72 ± 0.43 h (C15-rhG-CSF); AUC(0-t) 13,692.70 ± 307.98, 124,710.57 ± 7,418.19 and 24,322.13 ± 1,075.57 ng·h/mL; CL/f 1.46 ± 0.03, 0.16 ± 0.01 and 0.85 ± 0.03 L/h/kg; V/f 5.76 ± 0.72, 2.97 ± 0.22 and 6.96 ± 0.50 L/kg. Caveats: (1) the Results paragraph describing Tpeak is internally garbled ('serum concentration of C15-rhG-CSF reached peak was 2.15 ± 0.21 h, which was faster than that of rhG-CSF (2.15 ± 0.21 h)'), so Tmax values were taken from Table 1, which is self-consistent; (2) Methods describe centrifuged plasma samples while Results/Table 1 refer to serum half-life; (3) the efficacy section says 'seven groups with 12 mice in each group' but then lists eight groups; (4) the CTX dose is printed with rhG-CSF units, evidently a typographical error. C15-MAL itself was synthesized and characterized chemically (MW 307 Da, 98.0% purity) but was never administered or biologically tested alone, so it is not listed as an agent. No amino-acid sequence or SMILES appears in the body. The source file header lists 'PMID: ?'; the assigned PMID 35677307 was used.
